limits: No price refresh or alert mutation.

verdict: History tab inspected at both widths; it displays the same active alert card in this fixture.

observations.issue: History presents the active target/current-price card without dates or events, so its label suggests information the screen does not show.
observations.suggestion: If this tab is the union of active and triggered alerts, label it All. Reserve History for dated price/alert events.

strengths: Current/target comparison stays consistent with Active.
limits: Only one active alert exists in the review fixture; historical triggered events were not fabricated.

verdict: All four default favorites findings confirmed on a fresh route visit. Same unnamed mobile view buttons as the favorites redirect.
strengths: Default favorites state is consistent across both entry routes.
No viewport overflow.
limits: No favorites saved, removed or cleared.

verdict: List mode inspected at both widths. Desktop compact row works; mobile visibly overlaps.

observations.issue: At 390px the list row compresses the product-name column to 60px, while price copy and request/message controls overlay the product title and grower text. Multiple text layers collide inside the card.
observations.suggestion: Give the product identity a full-width row on mobile, with a small thumbnail beside it; place price and actions in separate rows below. Do not preserve the desktop multi-column row at this width.

strengths: Desktop list view makes much better use of width and shorter thumbnails.
limits: No favorite removed or message sent.

verdict: Second freshly reopened Recent tab confirms the one pass-one copy finding. Product row itself remains compact and sound.
strengths: Price and both actions fit on mobile.
No additional layout defect in this tab.
limits: No repeat request initiated.

verdict: Drawer list inspected at both widths; existing conversations were not opened because that marks messages read.

observations.issue: Desktop repeats Select a conversation in the pane heading, empty-state card, and composer placeholder while exposing pricing controls before a conversation is selected.
observations.suggestion: Use one centered Choose a conversation prompt; reveal the composer and relevant pricing actions after selection.

observations.issue: The permanent desktop footer explains You are messaging as Dispensary and Quotes set terms only; wholesale payment is handled directly in small text, adding role and settlement copy to every conversation.
observations.suggestion: Keep necessary settlement guidance beside a quote action or its confirmation, and remove the redundant role sentence.

strengths: Mobile conversation list is compact, readable, and fills the viewport cleanly.
Close action stays visible.
limits: Opening an existing conversation sends a read acknowledgement, so conversation contents and quote actions are excluded under the read-only constraint.

verdict: Desktop drawer inspected; this control is not present at the mobile breakpoint.

observations.issue: The recently used list names the visited shop Grower 001 instead of Vermont Nurseries, and prefixes familiar account pages with Dispensary.
observations.suggestion: Use the business name for shop visits and the same short Dashboard, Settings, and Saved labels as navigation.

strengths: Compact list fits its content without overlapping page controls.
limits: No mobile trigger exists in the current layout.

verdict: Fresh alternate layout inspected in both sizes; desktop readable, mobile severely clipped.

observations.issue: At 390px catalog List view keeps a desktop horizontal row: product-name columns shrink to 57–91px, pricing/message controls overlap text, prices disappear off the right edge, and Add buttons sit at x400–440 outside the 390px viewport. The document still reports 390px width because overflow is clipped internally.
observations.suggestion: Switch list rows to a mobile stack with a compact thumbnail beside full-width identity, then price/availability and full-width actions below. Assert that each price and action fits within the visible card.

strengths: Desktop list mode is readable and uses smaller thumbnails.
limits: No Add, favorite, alert, or messaging action submitted.

verdict: Additional 360x844 inspection confirms the existing copy/density findings without a new reflow defect.
strengths: Form fields use 16px text and remain within the 360px viewport.
No document-width overflow.
limits: Desktop and standard mobile baseline passes are separately captured; no inputs changed.
